div.div:
One release, in order
1 The image tag in order-worker.yaml changes and Flux applies it. 2 The controller derives build B and creates its Deployment and ScaledObject; B starts at one pod and polls, but gets no new work yet. 3 The controller ramps new workflow starts onto B through the Temporal API: 10 % for 30 s, 50 % for 30 s, then Current. Pinned runs never move. 4 KEDA scales each build on its own backlog, so B grows with new work while A falls back to its floor of one pod. 5 When the server reports A drained, the controller waits 1 h, sets A to 0 pods and deletes A's Deployment and ScaledObject on the next reconcile.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1280px; margin-left: 12px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #475569;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#475569, #9ba7b8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why nothing here is dashed
Every box exists during every release: build A and build B both run until A drains, and the extra pods KEDA adds are real pods. Dashes in this repo mean planned or optional, so a transient but deployed object is drawn solid and its lifetime is in its label. The sunset is the one replica write the controller keeps after handing replicas to KEDA (step 5), and it is written in the text rather than as an edge. checkout-abandon has the same objects (checkout-worker.yaml, checkout-abandon-scaler.yaml).
